newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end up on heating demand.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end up on heating demand.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended the week higher on expectations of early heating demand in parts of the northwestern U.S. when a very cool weather front moves into the region this weekend, market sources said.
"It's a little cooler. There's a little heating demand," said one Midwest-based power marketer.
Spot power prices in the western U.S. were also supported by firm regional natural gas prices and unplanned outages of several coal-fired units, brokers and marketers said.
October physical California-Oregon Border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) prices moved in line with futures, they said.
The scheduled shutdown of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit in Wintersburg, Ariz., was expected to provide support for October PV futures, market sources said.
"It will limit any downside," the marketer said.
The operator Arizona Public Service Co had planned to shut Palo Verde 1 Saturday for refueling for 45 days.
October COB futures settled up three cents at $15.47 a megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching as high as $15.60.
November COB ended down five cents at $16.45. Deferred COB months closed mixed.
October PV futures settled up 20 cents at $16.00 after traded between $15.85 and $16.10.
November PV ended unchanged from Thursday's settlement of $15.15. Outer-month PV contracts also closed flat.
